A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DataEnvGym work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original student-training results on GQA, MATH, and LiveCodeBench, alongside teacher-quality and skill-discovery experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original NaturalBench and MnMs results, generated-data accuracy measurements, and a data-versus-training ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 introduces a MnMs-specific adaptation: tool combinations become skills, and generation targets a random subset of skills without near-perfect student accuracy. The original teacher-student loop and three environment designs remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds NaturalBench and MnMs to GQA, MATH, and LiveCodeBench. NaturalBench expands visual evaluation to related image-question groups, while MnMs introduces tool planning and tool selection, extending coverage to a fourth domain.

E2.justification: Appendix E/Table 8 adds a first-iteration-data-only, longer-training comparator against full-data standard training. Existing With State/No State, oracle/inferred-skill, and GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini comparisons are retained; their extension to new benchmarks does not itself change comparator membership.

E3.justification: New protocols include NaturalBench question/image/binary/group scores, MnMs planning and tool metrics, evaluation of student n on data generated at n+1, and data-fraction/epoch controls. Figure 5's stopping description changes from sustained decline to sustained failure to improve, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained analyses, Appendix D/Figure 18 examines performance on newly generated, unseen data. Appendix E/Table 8 tests whether longer training on less data substitutes for additional data. Figure 5 also extends training trajectories and explicitly distinguishes post-peak behavior.

E5.justification: Figure 5 newly displays uncertainty-style shaded bands around training trajectories. Their statistical meaning and calculation are unspecified, and no run counts or seeds are supplied; the bands do not establish that additional repetitions occurred.

E6.justification: New results include NaturalBench group score reaching 6.00 from 0.00 with Open-Ended/With State, and MnMs plan accuracy reaching 75.96 from 37.30 with Skill-List/With State. Appendices D-E add further results, and Figure 5 revises trajectories. Original Tables 2-4 retain their values as v2 Tables 2, 5, and 6. Some new MnMs gains disagree with the printed scores.

T1.justification: The sequential-decision formulation and training, evaluation, and generation equations are retained. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs. The new epoch-rescaling example documents an experimental budget calculation rather than a theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion expand demonstrated support from three domains to four, explicitly including tool use and actions. The central contribution remains a modular, feedback-driven testbed for developing data generation agents.

C2.justification: v2 explains why standard skill discovery is poorly aligned with MnMs tools, interprets generated-data accuracy as evidence of a consistent but nontrivial teacher distribution, and argues that fresh data rather than longer training drives improvement. Existing interpretations of difficulty, rarity, and curriculum constraints remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4/Table 7 adds token costs, GPU times, and an A6000 hardware reference. Figure 16 supplies complete discovered skill lists, and Section 3.2 adds a repository pointer for new-task prompts and hyperparameters. Existing training recipes and prompt templates are retained; the externally referenced details are not available within the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds discussion of Learning to Simulate, MarioGPT, Todd et al.'s level generation, OMNI, and OMNI-EPIC; the new benchmarks also receive citations. These broaden the related-work context while preserving the teacher-focused positioning relative to environment generation and distillation.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact. v2 adds Section 3.2, a resource-cost subsection, Appendices D-E, and a short environment walkthrough, alongside targeted abstract/conclusion edits, renumbering, and punctuation or typo corrections.

P2.justification: v2 adds four substantive tables, a detailed loop diagram, complete skill-list displays, and a generated-data accuracy plot. Figure 5 is redrawn with changed axes, panel order, legend, shaded bands, and post-peak segments. Existing prompt and qualitative-example figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: Broader task evidence, a control addressing the contribution of additional data, and resource accounting improve empirical support and assessability over v1. The gains are limited by new reporting problems: inconsistent MnMs gain calculations, undefined Figure 5 bands, and Table 8's three-epoch GQA setting conflicting with the ten epochs retained in Appendix B.1.1.
